claim: The Royal Scots brought a Warrant for Lodge "Unity, Peace and Concord" when they relieved the 33rd in 1810.
quote: when the Royal Scots came to relieve the 33rd in 1810, thej^ brought with them their Warrant for Lodge " Unity, Peace and Concord " under which they had been working in Fort St. George, Madras.

claim: The regiment moved to Trichinopoly in 1812 and stayed there for two years.
quote: In 181 2 the regiment moved to Trichinopoly, where they remained two years, after which they again came to Secunderabad, where they remained till 1819, after which they moved to Wallajabad, and ultimately to England about the year 1824.

claim: No returns were made to the Grand Lodge of England from 1801 to 1820, leaving little record of Masonic activity in Hyderabad before 1822.
quote: from 1801 till 1820 no returns appear to have been made to the Grand Lodge of England, consequently very little beyond the bare facts above recorded can be gathered as to Masonry in Hyderabad previous to the establishment of Lodge "St. John" in 1822.

claim: Bro. Saunders was elected Worshipful Master for the coming year with Wor. Bro. Carrs as Treasurer.
quote: Bro. Saunders (no connection of the District Grand Master) was elected Worshipful Master for the coming year with Wor. Bro. Carrs, as Treasurer.

claim: Lodge Mayo applied to work in the St. John's building after previously working in Trimulgherry.
quote: An application was re- ceived from Lodge Mayo to be allowed to work in the St. John's building.

claim: The District Grand Lodge sanctioned the change allowing Lodge Mayo to work in Secunderabad.
quote: No objection however was raised and the change was eventually sanctioned.

claim: The Lodge Morland elected the Worshipful Master and Wardens of St. John's as Honorary Members.
quote: Lodge Morland, the new Scotch Lodge, having elected the Worshipful Master and Wardens of St. John's as Honorary Members, ' * a letter to this effect was read.

claim: Donations of Rs. 25 each were given to two orphanages and Rs. 50 to a widow of a deceased brother.
quote: The usual donations of Rs. 25 each to the two orphanages were given and a further grant of Rs. 50 to the widow of a deceased brother.

claim: A donation of Rs. 50 was sanctioned to a new native orphanage that had been lately opened.
quote: A donation of Rs. 50 was also sanctioned to a new native orphanage that had been lately opened.
